extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists, literature students, literary critics, creative-writing teachers
extracted.subtask_description: A framework for evaluating or teaching novels using E. M. Forster's seven universal aspects (story, people, plot, fantasy, prophecy, pattern, rhythm). Useful for critiquing, revising, or analyzing long-form fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story
rubrics_metrics.description: "A narrative of events arranged in their time-sequence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most primitive aspect: the sequence that answers 'and then? and then?' Story appeals to a reader's curiosity about what happens next. Useful as the basic skeleton of events; anti-patterns include a sequence of events that lacks interest or does not engage the reader's curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: People (Characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishes flat and round characters: flat characters are built around a single idea or quality and do not change; round characters are complex and develop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flat characters: can be summed up in one sentence, useful as foils, easy to remember. Round characters: 'capable of surprising in a convincing way' — they are complex, capable of surprising the reader convincingly, and develop/change over the course of the novel. Guidance implies favoring 'human truth' and depth in main characters; anti-patterns include relying only on flat types where sustained psychological truth is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative of events arranged with emphasis on causality; sharply distinct from story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example contrast: Story — 'The king died, and then the queen died.' Plot — 'The king died, and then the queen died of grief.' Plot demands the reader's intelligence and memory because it privileges causation and explanation over mere sequence. Anti-pattern: presenting events in time-sequence without causal links (story without plot).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fantasy
rubrics_metrics.description: The element of the marvellous, the supernatural, the impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fantasy asks the reader to grant something extra — a willing suspension of disbelief in the impossible. Use when the novel requires or benefits from marvellous or supernatural elements; anti-pattern: failing to establish the terms of the fantastical so the reader cannot suspend disbelief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophecy
rubrics_metrics.description: Not literal foretelling, but a tone of voice — a song or sense that the novelist gestures toward something universal beyond the literal events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prophecy is a tonal/voice quality that makes the work resonate beyond its plot and characters. Cited as present in authors such as Dostoevsky, Melville, Brontë, Lawrence. Guidance: cultivate a voice that suggests universality or larger truths rather than merely recounting events; anti-pattern: flat, purely literal narration that lacks a transcendent or prophetic tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: The aesthetic shape of the whole novel — its design as a unified object; more abstract than plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern arises from plot but is an abstract design of the novel as a whole. Can take shapes (e.g., hourglass-shaped as in Henry James's The Ambassadors, or chain-shaped). Guidance: attend to the overall architectural shape and unity of the work rather than only local causal sequences; anti-pattern: disjointed structure with no perceivable overall design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurrent themes, motifs, phrases that create internal music — like leitmotifs in Wagner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhythm includes 'easy rhythms' (recurrence within a book) and 'difficult rhythms' (the novel as a whole producing a symphonic effect, e.g., Tolstoy's War and Peace). Guidance: cultivate recurring elements that produce an internal music and propel the book's unity; anti-pattern: randomness or lack of recurrence that prevents the novel from achieving musical or thematic cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluative Criterion: Balance and primacy of pattern/rhythm and round characters
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest novels deploy all these aspects in balance, especially achieving rhythm and pattern without sacrificing the human truth of round characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or composing a novel, consider how the seven aspects are deployed together. Aim for a balance in which pattern and rhythm give the work aesthetic unity while round characters preserve human truth; avoid overemphasizing formal qualities (pattern/rhythm) at the expense of believable, developing characters.
